 Most recent Most popular Is City's honeymoon period over? published at 17:24 GMT 17:24 GMT 
 Nottm Forest v Man City (17:30 GMT) 
 Manchester City got back to winning ways in Europe in midweek after a three-game spell that included two league defeats - to Aston Villa and Brighton - and needing penalties to get past Brighton in the Carabao Cup.
 But even to do that they twice lost the lead and it all seemed like a bit of an uphill battle.
 After such a strong start to the season, has the bubble burst on Enzo Maresca's honeymoon period? Or can they recover?
 A big opportunity to return to winning ways in the league today against a struggling Forest side.

 Donnarumma dilemma published at 17:22 GMT 17:22 GMT 
 Nottm Forest v Man City (17:30 GMT) 
 Enzo Maresca continues to insist that Gianluigi Donnarumma is his number one, despite the goalkeeper making a number of mistakes in recent weeks.
 He was at fault for RB Leipzig's first goal, getting beaten at his near post, while there were a couple of other nervy moments that almost led to goals.
 It feels like Donnarumma is making a mistake in almost every game at the moment. City's last clean sheet in any competition was on 11 October against Liverpool (3-0) in the Premier League.

 Sixth manager incoming? published at 17:20 GMT 17:20 GMT 
 Nottm Forest v Man City (17:30 GMT) 
 "I will tell what we want to do, what we have to do. And if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround. And if not, the sixth manager will come in."
 Strong words last week from Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner, who seemed to suggest after the loss to Brentford that he would be heading for the exits if things do not turn around soon.
 His words of course refer to the fact that Forest had four different managers last season before appointing Glasner in the summer.
 With a notoriously impatient owner in Evangelis Marinakis, how long does Glasner have before his time at the City Ground is up?
 For the seventh time in nine matches in this Premier League campaign, Forest outperformed the opposing team in terms of xG, yet they have turned that dominant stat into just one win and six points in total.
 Forest, who have yet to score at home in any competition this season, have scored just six Premier League goals from an xG total of 14.34, an under-performance of 8.34 goals.
 That's comfortably the worst differential of any team this season, and the biggest under-performance by a side after nine Premier League games since at least 2021-22, when Opta introduced its revamped xG model.

 Anderson returns to old stomping ground published at 17:14 GMT 17:14 GMT 
 Nottm Forest v Man City (17:30 GMT) 
 Shamoon Hafez 
Football reporter at the City Ground 
 Elliot Anderson's stock has risen astronomically and there were considerable expectations on the midfielder's shoulders after sealing a £116m move from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City in the summer.
 European football expert Guillem Balague said on Match of the Day he had spoken to City manager Enzo Maresca in the summer and asked if he wanted to sign Bournemouth 's Alex Scott and Crystal Palace 's Adam Wharton.
 The Italian's response was "no", adding: "Anderson is going to become the key player for England, not just City."
 Anderson may well be afforded a generous reception when he makes his return to the City Ground on Saturday, with Nottingham Forest supporter Ellie Molloson telling BBC Sport: "I know the stadium will be ringing with 'Geordie Maradona'.
 "It will be bittersweet because we miss him, but we are quite proud of just how fantastic a player he is."
 But is Anderson managing to live up to the hype in the early days of his City career?
 The former Newcastle United player's tireless work-rate means he has effectively replaced Bernardo Silva and Rodri at Manchester City, making the step up to a side that won two trophies last season and could challenge for the title again.
 Though Anderson has not fully replicated the outright league-leading dominance he showcased across several metrics last season, his underlying numbers remain elite.
 He has drawn more fouls (28) than any other player in the division, while he ranks second for duels won (66) and third for successful passes (610) and touches on the ball (851).

 'We might see a Forest reaction here' published at 17:12 GMT 17:12 GMT 
 Nottm Forest v Man City (17:30 GMT) 
 Nottingham Forest just cannot score - they have managed only six league goals in their first nine games, the lowest total in the Premier League.
 Their manager, Oliver Glasner, got a bit stroppy after their defeat by Brentford last time out, saying he will make changes or he will end up being sacked. He tried the carrot approach at the start of the season but his team didn't bite - so now he is trying the stick.
 We might see a reaction here, and I do think Forest will score - Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma might even chuck one in for them, going off his recent poor form.
 It certainly won't be easy for City and they have their own issues at the moment after back-to-back league defeats, but I am still expecting them to create enough chances to win.
 Sutton's prediction: 1-2

 Darren Cann 
Former Premier League assistant referee on BBC Sport 
 On Havertz decision :
 In the 42 nd minute, Havertz had his shirt held in the penalty area. On review, Havertz was marginally in an offside position and as such, play was restarted with an indirect free kick for offside.
 The law states “if a player in an offside position moving towards the ball is fouled before playing the ball, the foul is penalised as it occurred before the offside offence.” (Note: In these situations the attacker hasn’t committed an offside offence until he challenges an opponent for the ball.)
 However, last season a similar situation arose when Brentford were awarded a penalty against Leeds, only for VAR to intervene as the Brentford player was offside.
 The previous season Newcastle were given a penalty after a VAR review against Bournemouth, despite the Newcastle player being in an offside position (but had not committed an offside offence before he was pulled back.)
 So this law can be interpreted differently in very similar situations and more consistency is required to deal with this complex and ambiguous law.

 Image source, Reuters Image caption, Rodrigo Muniz's last goal for Fulham was a stoppage-time equaliser at Brighton in August 2025
 By Sam Drury BBC Sport journalist Rodrigo Muniz scored his first goal since the opening day of last season as Fulham denied Newcastle and head coach Matthias Jaissle a much-needed win at Craven Cottage. 
 Jacob Murphy looked to have scored a stunning winner 10 minutes from time as he pounced on a loose pass inside the Fulham half before cutting inside and curling a left-foot shot into the far corner from 25 yards.
 But less than three minutes later, substitute Cesar Palacios' pass found its way to Muniz, who managed to stab the ball into the far corner.
 Both sides had late chances to win the game but Fulham keeper Bernd Leno denied Lewis Hall before Newcastle's Lukas Hornicek made a flying stop to keep out Ryan Sessegnon's stinging effort in stoppage time.
 The result means the visitors avoid a fifth defeat in six games to ease the pressure on Jaissle a fraction, but will feel it should have been three points having taken the lead late on.
 Meanwhile, Fulham extend their unbeaten run to four Premier League matches.
 Alvaro Arbeloa's side were the better team in the first half but struggled to create the chances to back that up, with Josh King, in his first appearance since earning a maiden England call-up, coming closest with a thumping 20-yard volley that Hornicek dived to push wide.
 By weight of chances, Newcastle should have been in front with Leno twice keeping out Harvey Barnes, on the second occasion with his face after the winger had sprinted clear.
 Dan Burn thought he had put the Magpies ahead from the resulting corner after turning in Murphy's cross.
 However, much to Newcastle's frustration, the goal was ruled out for Yoane Wissa holding Timothy Castagne off the ball, preventing the Fulham full-back from moving out to potentially play Burn offside.
 Barnes flashed another good chance wide just after the break before Sander Berge arrowed a shot inches past the post for Fulham.
 Newcastle had the better of the second period but the game seemed destined to end goalless before Murphy's fine strike led to a lively conclusion.
 More to follow.
